scope: Static analysis of usr/bin/mobile and bin/atcmdsrv from firmware 3.0.2 Build 241129 Rel.3n; no modem command was sent.

transport.client_behavior: mobile creates a stream socket and connects to a 110-byte sockaddr_un containing /tmp/atcmd

request.evidence: The send helper copies the caller's command, appends a literal carriage return, computes strlen, and requires write() to return that full length.

response.transport_behavior: raw stream reads into a caller-provided buffer with one byte reserved for NUL termination
response.note: The parser maps numeric CME/CMS final results to internal return codes. Exact handling of every unsolicited line remains unresolved.

server_evidence.atcmdsrv: The shipped server advertises an AT command server and contains Unix listen/accept paths plus /tmp/%s socket construction.
server_evidence.mobile_event_socket_distinction: /tmp/mobile_msg_server.sock is a separate AF_UNIX/SOCK_DGRAM endpoint and must not be confused with the /tmp/atcmd stream.

stub.policy: Exact argument-free query allowlist; deterministic synthetic values; ERROR for everything else; no forwarding or device access.
stub.privacy: Rejected commands are recorded only as a truncated verb, length, and SHA-256 digest so PINs, APNs, numbers, or message content cannot enter traces.

limits: The atcmdsrv-side per-client socket name selection has not been fully reconstructed.
Unsolicited result-code routing and concurrency behavior remain partially mapped.
A safe AT stub alone is insufficient authorization to launch mobile; network-manager, CP-reset/NVM-switch, and writable state boundaries remain gated.
